cells.tense: You are in the room where a vision gets turned into something you can do.
cells.ask: Pick the one connection you'd protect, and give it an hour this week that nothing else can take.
cells.core:
You're in the room where a vision gets turned into something you can do. Practice, repetition, the same small thing done again until it stops being effort. And you're in it with someone — the aloneness isn't loneliness here.

The practice is what makes the connection real. Anyone can feel a pull toward someone; you've built the strength to stay in it, to keep showing up and keep refining what you bring. That's why the connection holds when it's tested. Not because it's dramatic, but because you've done the reps. What you have is not an accident of feeling. It's made.
cells.sheetLine: The connection holds because you've done the reps.
cells.verb: letting a vision become something two can share
cells.place: where a thing is practiced until it comes without deciding

cells.tense: You keep rehearsing the moment the two of you will finally make it work.
cells.ask: Take one live connection as it is today, without the improvement plan.
cells.core:
Every session becomes a step toward a version of the connection that isn't here yet, and today's version keeps being treated as a draft.

When it's working, sharing is the reward, not a step toward one. The small thing done again, alone, becomes something the two of you do, and the doing is the point. The work stays a servant of what's already between you.

The work is real. It's also become the place where the connection lives, instead of the connection being the place where the work lives. What's coming is more practice, more preparation, more getting it right first. But the two of you don't arrive, because arriving keeps being scheduled for later.
cells.sheetLine: You're rehearsing the connection instead of having it.
cells.verb: letting a vision become something two can share
cells.place: where a thing is practiced until it comes without deciding

cells.tense: Something ended and you stopped sitting down with it to see what it held.
cells.ask: Sit with one thing that ended and write a single true line about it, no polish.
cells.core:
The practice that used to carry the thing ended when the thing did, and nothing took its place. You're not repeating anything now — the door closed and you're on the wrong side of it. What's gone quiet isn't the vision. It's the sitting down.

When it's working, the sessions run themselves: the same small thing done again, alone, until it starts to move on its own. You can already tell real from almost-real without checking. But the practice that would turn what you've lived into something you can stand on has thinned out, and you can't feel your way back to connection from the outside.
cells.sheetLine: The door closed and the practice went with it.
cells.verb: letting a vision become something two can share
cells.place: where a thing is practiced until it comes without deciding

cells.tense: You are already the thing two people use to find their way to each other.
cells.ask: Tell one person plainly what you actually did to make a connection work.
cells.core:
You are already what two people use to find their way to each other — showing up, small repairs nobody sees, the same few moves done again. You describe it as something that happened to you, or as luck.

Inside the doing, it feels ordinary: the appointment kept, the repair made, the unglamorous part handled. The practice is running. The accounting for it isn't. What would make it yours is saying it out loud — plain, once, to one person who's felt it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the bridge. You call it luck.
cells.verb: letting a vision become something two can share
cells.place: where a thing is practiced until it comes without deciding
